All — I reviewed BlueHarbor's redline and Alex's suggested compromise. Below are concrete drafting options and a recommended path to resolution so we can return a single consolidated document to BlueHarbor by EOD tomorrow.

Option A (preferred, low risk to Redwood):
- Governing law: California law governing the Agreement.
- Forum/Equitable relief carveout: Add carveout exactly as Alex proposed but add a short notice requirement: "Notwithstanding any agreement to arbitrate, either Party may seek injunctive or other provisional relief in a court of competent jurisdiction to protect its confidential information or to prevent irreparable harm, provided that the Party seeking relief shall, to the extent practicable, notify the other Party and allow 48 hours' notice for discussion unless such notice would frustrate the purpose of the relief."
- Arbitration: JAMS, seat in San Francisco; maintain final determination of damages in arbitration. Emergency arbitrator clause optional but recommended.

Rationale: Keeps Redwood's operational and precedent base in CA, preserves rapid access to court for urgent IP/data-protection issues, and limits venue shopping via the notice gate.

Option B (conservative concession for strategic deal):
- Governing law: New York law for the Agreement (BlueHarbor preference).
- Include same equitable relief carveout.
- Add mutual forum-selection provision for enforcement of court-ordered provisional relief (i.e., if provisional relief is granted in a local court, enforcement proceedings limited to the issuing court).

Recommended action: Offer Option A in the next redline with an explicit paragraph offering Option B if BlueHarbor can accept a mutual waiver of jury trial and a one-time signing credit (commercial concession).

I have drafted the exact language in the attached PDF (MSA_clause_compare.pdf) and can produce a tracked-word redline for our next pass.

Questions: 1) Karthik — do you foresee any product implications for the provisional relief carveout? 2) Alex — do you want me to include a one-sentence commercial concession to support Option B (e.g., $10k one-time credit)?
